about: Every component the 2026-09-30 inventory of the film project found (306), and where each one lives in Slate now. `category` is the inventory's own class, kept verbatim; `destination` is Slate's decision, so the two can differ, and the counts below show where. Source paths keep the original reference (relative to FILMROOT, or on this Mac); names and reasons are written brand-neutral, because no company specific becomes a Slate default. This file maps components. knowledge/lessons.json maps the rules and lessons inside them.

source.readers: visual-engine (ve), sound-voice (sv), ae-qa-delivery (aq), process-lessons (pl), and the coverage pass's missed components (cm); ids are reader prefix plus the index in that reader's list

harvest: First harvest, 2026-09-30. It runs again once films B and C and the p3 sound are approved. sound/p3/ and the film's newer memory notes postdate the inventory and are picked up then. Two classes were overtaken by events the same morning: SOUND.md (pl-015) and sound/proofs/ (cm-029) were classed obsolete before the film went back to proof 2 as its sound reference; their destinations follow the plan, not the stale class.

statuses.ported: Slate uses it as it is: the code or file comes over with only paths, names and settings wired to film.json, the brand pack or config. For a vendor tool or skill, Slate depends on it unchanged: installed and pinned, never copied.
statuses.generalized: Slate rebuilds it with brand and film specifics pulled out into brand packs, film.json, formats or config (or, for a doc, rewrites it brand-neutral in a skill reference).
statuses.dropped: Slate doesn't carry it. The reason says why, and where anything worth keeping went: a lesson in the knowledge ledger, a template in a skill, the private TrueSpace pack, or golden-test data read in place.

modules: A destination module is a path from ARCHITECTURE section 2, or, for a dropped component that nothing in the repo stands in for, one of the two places outside the core below. An entry whose module is `tests` is film data that golden tests read in place from FILMROOT (ARCHITECTURE section 10); nothing is copied into Slate.

outside_the_core.FILMROOT (left in place): Stays in the film project, untouched. Nothing is copied or moved.
outside_the_core.~/code/slate-brands (private TrueSpace p: Company content for the private TrueSpace pack in ~/code/slate-brands (ARCHITECTURE sections 1 and 3: PERSONAL only, never pushed). It never enters ~/code/slate.

checks: Every inventory record (5 readers, 306 records) appears exactly once, by id.
Every entry has a destination with a non-empty module, a status of ported, generalized or dropped, and a reason.
A module is an ARCHITECTURE section 2 path or one of the outside-the-core destinations above.
Names and reasons carry no brand names, colours, voice ids, font kits, sample data or banned words.
The category counts match the plan (81, 127, 54, 28, 16).

destination.reason: Slate's engine has its own manifest: Remotion pinned exactly at 4.0.521, esbuild declared, and the declared-but-unused packages (framer-motion, postprocessing, @react-three/postprocessing, @remotion/motion-blur) and the broken render script left out. Each dependency's decision is in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md.

The core renderer: sub-frames averaged in 16-bit straight into ProRes 422 HQ 10-bit BT.709, lossless transport, frame ranges, bundle deleted on exit. The hard-coded 30000/1001 and entry move to film.json and the generated per-film entry.
The engine's `stills` command: many stills from one bundle, as is, plus the bundle cleanup it lacked (it left its temp bundle behind).

v2 tooling (HANDOVER.md section 5). The need it served, checking a revision against the approved version by measurement, is part of perfect-don't-replace and the review packet.
